protections: Entry names written into server-built archives (zip/tar*) must not contain a component that an extractor can read as a parent or absolute path; on a Linux host a literal backslash in an on-disk filename passes through unchanged into NameInArchive (filepath.ToSlash only rewrites the host separator).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: public share download looks like a separate unauthenticated feature, but it calls the same rawDirHandler/getFiles, so a fix in getFiles closes it

rewriting backslash to '/' looks like it 'normalises' the name, but for a file literally named with '..\' segments it turns those into real '../' entry segments, so the check has to run after the conversion

a solver may reject backslash names at creation time and consider the archive safe; that is insufficient (files placed on disk out-of-band or existing before the fix still reach getFiles via Readdirnames) and breaks legitimate Linux filenames

conflicts.what: if the fix just rewrites every backslash to '/', a file named with literal '..\' becomes a real '../' traversal (T3); if it rejects or drops any name containing a separator, nested directory entries that use the real '/' separator (and the host separator that ToSlash converts on Windows) stop working (T5)
refusing to create backslash filenames on upload/rename/mkdir conflicts with keeping legitimate Linux filenames that contain a backslash working

fairness_risks: Backslash is a legal filename character on Linux; a rule that refuses to create such files (resource.go:133/163/374, tus_handlers.go:88), or that fails the whole archive download, would contradict existing must-keep-working behaviour. Hidden tests should expect the file to be included under a safe entry name, or skipped, rather than a 500 error for the whole download.
Nested directories must still show up in the archive as '/'-separated entries (raw.go:150-152, 127); a check that refuses any name containing a separator would break normal downloads.

The exact replacement for a backslash ('_', '/' followed by cleaning, or skipping the entry) is a design choice; tests should only assert that no entry has a '..' or absolute segment when read with either '/' or '\' as the separator, plus that normal files are present.

design.why: Only one independent fix site exists (the NameInArchive computation in getFiles, raw.go:125-127); the authenticated route (raw.go:109) and the public-share route (public.go:131) both go through it, and the conversion shape (T3) and the coupled separator (T5) are properties of that single fix. T4 is a decoy fix site, not a required one. With at most one real independent group there is no deepseek-type trap (no route where the protection is absent with a reason to dismiss) and the candidate cannot reach 3-5 independent traps. Best use: a single-trap task whose hidden tests cover T3+T5 shapes (literal '..\' name, nested dirs, both routes).

The ToSlash conversion line looks like it comes from 9595f39 (CHANGELOG.md:260, Dec 2025), which is earlier than A.
That the upstream B fix (8503ba61ff51) changed only http/raw.go and did not bump github.com/mholt/archives (raw.go:13).
That mholt/archives writes NameInArchive verbatim, without its own sanitisation, for both the Zip and Tar archivers (raw.go:51-67, 205).

Out of scope, not recorded as a trap: getFiles uses Stat/Open, which follow symlinks (raw.go:117, 133, 139), so symlinks under a share root may be archived; this is a separate protection that is not in the candidate's advisories.
The Content-Disposition archive name (raw.go:187-203) can contain a backslash from filepath.Base, but url.PathEscape is expected to encode it; not treated as a trap.
